content.text: I’ll review the existing Project structure and live pages, then propose a compact design that keeps Project above Themes and fits the shared Work layout.

There is already a Project-level foundation, including a structure contract and a dedicated design Block. That Block also retains older proposals, so I’m checking them against the live pages before treating them as current design.

The live Project page already has MindMap, Findings, Themes and Status. Its Work page is still a long directory-style list, and status mostly summarizes Questions and Tasks. The main gap is a clear account of how the Themes depend on each other and what the Project is ready to deliver.

**Yes—we have a Project foundation, but its interface is behind the newer Work and Paper designs.** This chat can serve as the dedicated Project design session.

Project remains the parent:

```text
Project
└─ Theme
   └─ Block → Job → Task → Run
```

I inspected the live Project-Ladder page, its Paper Theme container, the shared Work frame, and their source contracts.

**What exists today**

- [Project-Ladder](http://100.121.165.84:5623/_board/workbench?path=blueprints%2FProject-Ladder&layout=focus) has a mission, Theme navigation, and Report views: **MindMap · Findings · Themes · Status**.
- Project Delivery already collects deliveries from below, with their origins.
- Theme pages use the same generic views. The Paper Theme still says **Themes**, although its children are Boards; its map starts `paper → paper`, and it has no visible Purpose.
- Project and Theme Work pages remain directory-style lists. They have not adopted the newer **Review Content / Around the Work** arrangement.
- [b10_project_workbench](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/blueprints/Project-Ladder/work/b10_project_workbench/board.md) holds the existing design questions. Its scratch drawing is explicitly exploratory, with no recorded decisions. Older six-Space proposals should be treated as history.

The missing piece is **Project coordination**: how its mission connects to the Themes, which outputs cross between them, what is waiting on a decision, and which deliverables satisfy the Project’s intended outcome.

**My proposed view map**

Keep the shared Work frame and its four view names. Give Project and Theme different content within that frame:

| View | Project sections | Theme sections |
|---|---|---|
| **Overview** | Mission · Outcomes · Themes · Dependencies | Purpose · Blocks · Dependencies |
| **Status** | Themes · Waiting | Blocks · Waiting |
| **Findings** | Findings grouped by Theme, linked to their evidence | Findings grouped by Block, linked to their evidence |
| **Delivery** | Project handover · Block deliveries | Block deliveries |

“Dependencies” shows the relationship; “Waiting” shows the unresolved condition. For example:

```text
Work Block ── estimates v1 ──▶ Paper evidence Job
                                  waiting for review
```

Each connection must open the actual producer, artifact and consumer. A declared requirement without a bound artifact should say **unbound**; the interface should never infer a dependency from folder names.

Under every view, reuse the current shared **Around the Work** group:

**Studio · Interactions · Decisions · Things to Know · Checklist · Timeline · Skills · Files**

Project decisions can live at Project level. Theme pages aggregate their Blocks’ records and retain the source link; the current contract says a Theme groups work and owns no Studio topics.

**How this connects to skills**

| UI responsibility | Owning contract |
|---|---|
| Project identity, mission, profiles and Theme boundary | [haipipe-project](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/skills/1_base/project/haipipe-project/SKILL.md) |
| Shared frame, sections and interactions | [haipipe-ui](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/skills/1_base/workbench/haipipe-ui/SKILL.md), with the current [Work frame decisions](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/skills/2_theme/work/workbench-work/SKILL.md:23) |
| Findings and evidence | `haipipe-report` plus each Theme’s owner |
| Studio and recorded decisions | `haipipe-studio`; questions/forms use `haipipe-interaction` |
| Deliverables and handover state | `haipipe-delivery` plus the producing Theme’s contract |

For the design matrix, I would use **Project and Theme as two page-type columns**, with the four views as rows. Each cell would list its sections, owning skills and actual examples. Research/software/hybrid remain Project profiles unless their content proves a distinct interface is necessary.

One contract inconsistency also needs resolving: the main Project skill requires `project.md`, while its structure reference still calls `README.md` required. A dedicated Project/Theme view contract should reconcile that and explicitly own dependency aggregation.

My recommendation is to begin with **Project → Overview**: mission, intended outcomes, Themes and their connections. That gives the rest of the interface a clear organizing purpose.

No files or services were changed. This was a desktop review; mobile behavior remains unverified.

Yes—I get it. **The Project page should explain the plan through its Themes.** Remove the **Work / Report** split, use **Themes as the view buttons**, and use **sections within each Theme view** to explain its plan. I’m reading “session” here as “section.”

For the page in your screenshot:

```text
Proj11-CGM-FM

Project   Work   Discovery   Insight   Paper   …

MISSION
Study scaling laws and pretraining objectives for CGM foundation models.
```

**Project** gives the overall plan and connections between Themes. The other buttons show only Themes present in this Project. **Work** here names the computational Theme.

Inside a Theme view, I suggest:

| Section | What it explains |
|---|---|
| **Purpose** | What this Theme contributes to the Project’s mission |
| **Plan** | How we intend to achieve that contribution—the steps and their order |
| **Blocks** | The actual work carrying out that plan, with each Block’s goal and current state |
| **Handoffs** | What this Theme needs from others and what it supplies |

The **Plan should use the Theme’s own language**, rather than repeat the same generic checklist everywhere. For example, these are illustrative plans—not claims about what your Project already contains:

| Theme button | Plan shown inside |
|---|---|
| **Work** | Prepare data → pretrain → evaluate scaling → compare objectives |
| **Discovery** | Define questions → find prior work → assess evidence → synthesize |
| **Insight** | Frame questions → connect results → interpret findings |
| **Paper** | Establish the claim → organize evidence → develop the story → write |

Each step opens the Blocks responsible for it. An unassigned step stays visibly **unassigned**, so the page can explain the intended plan before all the work exists.

Below that, keep the shared **Around the Work** sections for Studio, Interactions, Decisions, Checklist, and the other supporting material.

This changes the organizing question from “am I working or reporting?” to **“which part of this Project am I planning and understanding?”** The plan, current work and resulting evidence then stay together in that Theme’s view.

找到了，在当前打开的 Obsidian vault **Project-ObsidianVault** 中：

[Weekly Report Nov-16 一些基本的思考.md](</Users/jluo41/Desktop/jluo41-repo/examples-A7-notes/Project-ObsidianVault/Weekly Report Nov-16 一些基本的思考.md>)

内容包括 **Element / Brick、版本历史、评价与反馈、AI 自动迭代，以及 Paper Theme** 的思考。

你是怎么想的
我再看一下这篇笔记后面关于 Element 和 Brick 的部分，把你的原意和我的建议分开。
我觉得这个thought 还是不是很成熟 你能不能详详细细的看一下整个repo 仔仔细细的思考一下啊
可以。我先不急着给 Element、Brick 下定义，也不改代码。我会把仓库里的存储结构、页面呈现、Run 执行、Studio／Chat，以及反馈和版本记录串起来看，找出它们实际怎样配合、哪里还互相矛盾，再判断“一体两面”这个想法能不能成立。
先看到一个重要变化：仓库里已经开始把 Brick 定义成“可评论、可修改、可追溯的内容”，并且做了跨页面共用的地址和卡片机制。所以这次需要判断的，不只是 Folder 和 UI 怎么对应，还包括这套内容机制是否已经统一、哪些地方仍然只是文档中的约定。我会继续对照实际代码和各个 Theme。

现在更清楚了：BJTR 在不同 Theme 里承载的含义并不一样——Paper 的 Job 可以是一版稿件，Insight 的 Job 是问题版本与数据版本的组合，Labeling 又区分“确定含义”和“执行含义”。因此，同一套文件夹骨架可以共用，但不能直接推出同一套内容结构或工作流程。

另一个关键点是：仓库已有 Folder／Element／Session 三视图的约定。我正在检查它与新加入的 Brick 概念是否接得上，尤其是版本变化后，评论、人工确认和历史还能不能准确指向原来的内容。

我找到一个能检验这套想法的具体例子：共享段落卡片会保存“人确认过的原文”，但正文改掉后，仍可能显示旧的 ✓；同一段落换到另一个 View，卡片地址又会变化。这两点我已用临时数据复现。它们说明，内容的身份、版本和页面位置还没有完全分开。

另外，现有的 23 项卡片、Session 和 Elements 相关测试都通过了。这也提示我们：组件能正常显示，还不足以证明“同一个内容经过修改、搬动和复用后仍能追溯”。后者才是这次架构需要补上的核心。

我仔细看过以后，觉得你的“一体两面”抓住了方向，但**“一体”目前还没有定义清楚**。如果现在直接把它定成 Folder-System 和 UI-System，后面很容易继续遇到同一种问题：页面看起来统一了，内容、版本、评论和工作过程却没有真正接起来。

我现在倾向于这样理解：

**“体”是持续积累的工作及其内容；文件系统负责保存，UI 负责呈现和操作。Brick 是其中可被讨论和修改的内容，Session 是推动它发生变化的过程。**

这次我检查了三个第一方 package 的定位、四个 Blueprint Project、七个 Theme 的主要契约，并追到了共享页面、卡片、地址、Run、Studio 和 Session 的实现与测试。重点是与你这个问题有关的架构链路，没有逐行审完所有上游 `references/`。没有修改仓库。

下面是我比较完整的判断。

**1．首先，你现在列出来的东西，实际上属于不同维度。**

例如：

```text
examples → Project → Theme → Block → Job → Task → Run
```

这是归属和工作组织。按照当前仓库，Project 在 Theme 上面，`examples-*`、`blueprints` 是容纳 Project 的目录。

而：

```text
Page → View → Section → Row / Card / Tab
```

是页面组织。

再比如：

```text
研究问题 → 主张 → 段落 → 句子
                   ↘ 引用、数值、图表
```

是内容组织。

这些结构有联系，但不能接成一条大树。

你笔记里的：

> PaperBlock > Paper Version > Task Draft > View Draft > Section DraftLab > Sentence

作为“从哪里找到一句话”的导航路径很有用。但作为句子的身份定义，就有问题：一句话移到另一个 View，或者同时出现在 Draft 和 Review 里，它还是同一句话。

**所以，页面位置应该指向内容，不能决定内容是谁。**

仓库已经意识到这一点：[三视图契约](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/servers/workbench/ref/three-views.md)明确写了 Folder 与 Element 是多对多关系。这比“一个文件夹对应一个页面区域”更接近实际情况。

**2．BJTR 是共用骨架，但每个 Theme 给这套骨架赋予了不同含义。**

这是通读几个 Theme 后，最值得保留的设计。

| Theme | 当前组织方式体现的重点 |
|---|---|
| Work | Task 和 Run 生产计算结果、证据 |
| Paper | 写作 Job 对应一次稿件版本／发送，证据 Jobs 可以被多个版本共用 |
| Insight | Question Book 保存问题与代码；Board Job 绑定问题版本和数据版本 |
| Design | Method Book 保存方法；Job 绑定目标、方法版本和输入版本 |
| Labeling | 区分确定标签含义、实现标签规则、执行冻结规则 |
| Discovery | 获取、检查、综合外部证据 |
| CoWork | 围绕人、请求、会议和交付组织工作 |

这意味着，**统一的对象边界可以成立，统一的工作步骤不一定成立。**

例如，Paper 的一句话、Insight 的一个回答、Labeling 的一条规则，都可以接受评论、保留历史。但它们怎样被验证、谁能确认、修改后影响什么，必须由各自 Theme 决定。

因此，共享层适合统一：

- 如何找到对象及其来源。
- 评论、修改建议、确认记录如何保存。
- 怎样引用其他对象与特定版本。
- 页面如何展示这些关系。

每个 Theme 继续负责自己的内容含义、执行方式和完成条件。

**3．Brick 应该属于工作内容本身，放在 UI-System 下面会限制它。**

仓库已经有一份相当具体的 [Brick 设计](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/skills/2_theme/paper/haipipe-paper/ref/bricks.md)：一个 Brick 有内容文件、记录卡片、页面展示三个落点。

这个方向我赞同。即使没有打开浏览器，句子、研究问题、设计方案仍然存在；AI 也应该能通过文件操作它们。

我建议暂时用下面这个区别：

| 概念 | 回答的问题 | 例子 |
|---|---|---|
| Brick | 我们正在讨论、修改或判断什么？ | 一个主张、一条规则、一句正文、一项设计 |
| UI Element | 用什么形式呈现和操作它？ | 段落、表格行、折叠卡片、侧栏标签 |

同一个 Brick 可以有不同呈现；一个表格也可以呈现多个 Brick。

这里还有一个容易混淆的特殊情况：在设计 workbench 的 Blueprint 中，“这个 tab 应该怎么工作”本身就是研究对象。此时可以评论这个 tab 的**设计定义**。这不意味着所有用户页面上的 tab 都要成为带独立生命周期的 Brick。

另外，我不建议把所有东西都强行变成 Brick。计算文件、运行日志、原始数据行、按钮，都不需要自动拥有评论、评分和人工确认。

比较实用的判断是：

> 这个东西是否需要被独立讨论、修改、引用或判断？

有这个需要，再赋予它稳定的内容身份。

**4．“把每个 Brick 做好，就做好了 Delivery”，还差了一个非常重要的条件：关系。**

这是我对笔记里最想补充的一点。

每个句子单独都通顺，整篇论文仍然可能：

- 前后矛盾。
- 重复表达。
- 没有回答研究问题。
- 用正确的数字支持了不成立的推论。
- 缺少连接证据和结论的关键一步。

所以质量至少要判断三件事：

```text
内容本身是否成立
        +
内容之间的关系是否成立
        +
整个交付是否完成了目的
```

你的“雕塑”类比里，除了砖的质量，还要有砖怎样组成结构，以及整个结构是否符合设计。

仓库其实已经有这种关系的基础：

- Paper 的句子引用 Evidence。
- Insight 的回答依赖问题版本与数据版本。
- Design 读取签署的 Insight handoff。
- Labeling 的执行依赖冻结的 meaning。

因此，下一步值得明确的，不只是 Brick 类型表，还包括：

- `part-of`：它组成什么？
- `supports / refers-to`：它支持或引用什么？
- `depends-on`：什么变化会让它需要重新检查？
- `derived-from`：它从哪个结果、哪个版本产生？

**Folder 可以是树；内容和证据的关系需要允许成网。**

**5．现在最缺的，是把“身份、版本、位置、判断”分开。**

这一点已经不只是理论问题。我用临时数据复现了两个现象：

- 一段文字被人工 ✓ 确认后，正文换成不同结论，共享段落渲染仍然显示原来的 ✓。
- 同一个 `p1` 从 Findings 移到 Overview，地址从 `findings.p1` 变成 `overview.p1`，原来的卡片关联不会自然跟过去。

对应实现是 [段落卡片](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/servers/workbench/page/paragraph_cards.py)和[共享标记](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/servers/workbench/page/item_marks.py)。

这说明，至少要回答四个不同的问题：

| 问题 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| 它是谁？ | 内容持续存在的身份 |
| 它现在是什么？ | 当前内容版本 |
| 它在哪里？ | 所属文件、锚点和展示位置 |
| 谁判断过什么？ | 对特定版本、按特定标准作出的评价或确认 |

尤其是最后一项：**✓ 应该意味着“这个版本被确认过”，不能只是“这个地址曾经被点过”。**

同样，★ 应该能追到评价的版本和 rubric；上游证据改变后，下游旧评价是否仍适用，也必须有规则。

现有 Brick 文档已经把跨版本 lineage、上游变化后的 stale、拆分合并等列为待办。这些是关键语义，优先级高于继续增加更多标记或页面组件。

**6．Studio、Chat、Session 都需要，但各自保存的东西应该不同。**

我建议按“什么需要留下来”区分它们：

- **Chat**：进行讨论和发出行动请求的入口。
- **Session**：一次持续工作的上下文，可以跨多个对象、多个 Run。
- **Episode**：这次工作中一个有意义的推进过程，记录目标、修改、理由和涉及的对象。
- **Studio topic**：长期讨论的一个问题，积累方案、图、决定和未决问题。

一个 Studio topic 可以经历多个 Session；一个 Session 也可以推进多个 topic。

所以你前面说“用 session 解释每个 Theme 的 plan”，我理解，而且可以做。但需要进一步分开：

**Session 解释这次为什么这样推进；当前有效的计划，仍然应该保存在它所属的 Project、Block 或 Job。**

否则，换一个 Session 后，人又要重新翻聊天才能知道现在究竟按哪个计划做。

仓库现在已经有这个方向：[Session 实现](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/servers/workbench/page/frame_sessions.py)从 Run passes、Studio passes 和 Draft review passes 读取 episode，而不是只展示原始聊天记录。

但这里目前主要接通了文件夹级关联。三视图契约也明确承认，各 Theme 的 Element 映射、内容旁的 Session 关联，还有部分没有完成。

**7．AI 的 loop 应该围绕“可采取的行动及其依据”，不能只围绕评分。**

你说的“大浪淘沙，只把最关键的问题留下”，我认为是整个想法里最有价值的目标。

但“低分就改，高分就结束”还不够。不同内容需要不同的闭环：

- 语句不通顺：可以重写，检查是否更清楚且保持原意。
- 数字不一致：回到对应 Result 核对。
- 证据缺失：寻找证据，或委托新的工作。
- 研究目标有分歧：需要人作选择。
- 多个局部都合理、整体却冲突：需要整体层面的审阅。

同一句话可能同时涉及以上几种情况。因此，现有 Brick 文档里的 `Choice / Prose / Fact / Input`，适合作为处理方式的起点；我暂时不会把它们定成互斥、不可变化的类型继承树。

更稳妥的是把以下两项分开：

**它是什么类型的内容；这次修改涉及什么判断、谁有权作出判断。**

目前 [Paper Draft workflow](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/plugins/haipipe-toolkit/skills/2_theme/paper/haipipe-paper-draft/ref/workflow.md)已经比简单评分循环成熟：有独立评价、盲 A/B、原意检查、无改进停止和不确定时留下评论。值得推广的是这些原则，而不是把 Paper 的“8 分通过”推广到所有 Theme。

你真正要优化的，应该是**人在什么地方投入注意力最有价值**。同一个上游决定影响十句话时，最好集中成一个有来由、有影响范围的决定，而不是弹出十张相同问题的卡片。

then how to we present the chat-sessions? how do we save it?
I’ll check how sessions are saved today, then map out a clear way to show the conversation, the work it changed, and the decisions worth keeping.

The repo currently has two separate pieces: a saved-chat exporter and a work-history viewer built from passes. They aren’t fully connected yet. I’d keep one archive per conversation, then link each meaningful episode to the files and Bricks it changed. That lets the UI show the same history from either the session or the content.

I’d present **one conversation as a series of meaningful episodes**, while saving the original conversation once. I drew a [fourth concept image](/Users/jluo41/Desktop/Tools-SPACE/output/imagegen/work-concept-2026-11-19/04-sessions-and-records.png) showing this.

**How we present it**

Put **Sessions inside Timeline**, scoped to the current Project, Theme or Block.

For example, our current conversation could appear as:

```text
Understanding the workbench concept
├─ Examine the repository
├─ Clarify Folder, UI and Brick
├─ Draw the concept
└─ Design how sessions are preserved
```

These are episodes within one chat. Clicking an episode opens:

- **Ask:** what were we trying to resolve?
- **Change:** what was created or modified?
- **Reason:** why did we choose this approach?
- **Connections:** affected files, Bricks, versions and decisions.

“View source” opens the relevant conversation passage. “Continue discussion” returns to the chat when available.

A Brick’s 🧵 opens this **same history filtered to that Brick**. Project-level history aggregates those records.

**How we save it**

I propose two linked records:

```text
<owner>/studio/chat/<session>/
├─ session.yaml       identity and original chat reference
├─ events.jsonl       available original messages and tool events
├─ transcript.md      readable conversation, generated from events
└─ assets/            saved images and attachments

<work>/runs/<run>/passes/<pass>/
└─ pass.md            one meaningful episode
```

The conversation archive has one declared home. If the chat touches several Blocks, those Blocks link to it.

Each episode records:

```text
Session identity + source message range
Goal and outcome
Changed files and Brick addresses
Before / after versions
Reasons and links to decisions
```

**The session title can change; its identity should remain stable.** Use the provider and native session ID to identify it.

Decisions and accepted content stay in their owning files. The episode explains and links to them.

**When we save**

I’d save incrementally:

- After each completed turn: checkpoint newly available conversation events.
- After a meaningful piece of work: save its episode.
- Before a handoff or interruption: checkpoint unfinished work.
- On resuming: continue from the saved cursor without duplicating messages.

That avoids relying on a final “save this chat” step.

**What exists today**

The repo already exports registered Claude chats into a readable transcript and simple digest, and displays work episodes from passes. The exporter summarizes tool activity; it is not a complete raw archive. Conversation-based grouping, reliable links to exact messages and Bricks, and a provider-neutral capture path—including Codex—still need implementation.

for you what is your element UI and brick for makeing the UI? do you get what I mean?

Yes—you mean **when the UI itself is our deliverable, what are the Elements and Bricks that we design, build and improve?**

For that, I’d treat **Element and Brick as two ways of looking at a meaningful UI part**:

- **UI Element:** its visible form and interaction—what the person sees and operates.
- **Brick:** that part as something we develop—with a purpose, implementation, evaluation, versions and feedback.

Using the **Sessions UI** we just discussed:

| UI Element on screen | The Brick we develop | What makes it good? |
|---|---|---|
| Session list with expandable episodes | **Session navigator** | Can I find the conversation and the relevant episode? |
| Episode detail showing Ask → Change → Reason | **Episode reader** | Can I quickly understand what happened and why? |
| Before/after comparison | **Change viewer** | Can I see exactly what changed, against which version? |
| Links to content, evidence and original chat | **Source navigator** | Can I reach the correct source and return without losing context? |

**An individual button usually belongs inside one of these Bricks.** We give a unit its own Brick when it has a coherent responsibility that we can independently design and judge.

For example:

```text
Brick: Episode reader
│
├─ Purpose       Understand one episode
├─ Inputs        Episode record + linked content
├─ UI elements   Heading, summary, diff, evidence links
├─ Behaviour     Expand, inspect, follow source
├─ Implementation
│                Renderer, styles and data reader
├─ Evaluation    Clear? Accurate? Sources reachable?
└─ History       Versions, feedback, decisions
```

These would reference the actual design and code files.

**Then there is type versus instance:**

```text
Episode reader — reusable component
    ├─ displays “Examine the repository”
    ├─ displays “Draw the concept”
    └─ displays “Design session storage”
```

Changing the **Episode reader’s design** can improve all three instances. Changing the **content of one episode** affects that episode.

So our UI-building process becomes:

**Choose the user’s task → define meaningful UI Bricks → arrange their Elements → build → evaluate each Brick and the whole page → revise.**

For this conversation, our Bricks would be things such as **Session navigator** and **Episode reader**. Those are the things you could comment on—“this hides the reason,” “this comparison is unclear”—and I would revise while preserving their design history.
